bug_semantics: uuid v3()/v5() (shared helper src/v35.ts) and v6() accept a caller-supplied output buffer and offset, then copy 16 UUID bytes with buf[offset+i]=bytes[i] and return buf, without rejecting offset<0 or offset+16>buf.length. On Uint8Array, out-of-range index assignment is a silent no-op, so a too-small buffer or too-large offset yields a mixed/truncated identifier (new bytes plus stale tail) with no exception. v1()/v4()/v7() already throw RangeError on the same bounds, so callers that treat a returned buffer as a complete 16-byte UUID get integrity failures only on v3/v5/v6. This is CWE-787/CWE-1285 in JS typed-array terms (silent partial write), not a native memory smash.
flaw_origin: v5() grew buf/offset parameters in 1d56dc9e80774f651602c53899a5f63cc304ed0f but ignored them (return buf || stringify). The first actual 16-byte copy into the caller buffer is PR #201 member 37a5efa8b8a7050911a89f8ae1d02be5a7ee2fc0, which added an unguarded loop in v5.js matching contemporaneous v4.js style. That loop was extracted into lib/v35.js (and reused for new v3()) by dc02a760a56e0cb22e743ccf42fb2d71cba63882, restyled, then ported to src/v35.ts by 1e0f9870db864ca93f7a69db0d468b5e1b7605e7. v6() independently first-wrote the same unguarded copy in c4ed13e7159d87c9e42a349bdd9dc955f1af46b6. e0ee90051ebd13475bbcff4d371330aa4f9bd1dd later added the RangeError guard only to v1/v4/v7; it did not write the v3/v5/v6 loops and is not the BIC.
